Acer palmatum.facts: Famous for its hand-shaped leaves, it has been cultivated in Japan for centuries and is a symbol of elegance.

Cedrus deodara.facts: The national tree of Pakistan, its name comes from Sanskrit meaning 'Timber of the Gods'.

Celtis sinensis.facts: The small round fruits are edible and were historically used by children as ammunition for bamboo pea shooters.

Cinnamomum camphora (Linn) Presl.facts: Every part of this tree smells like camphor; it is an evergreen that can live for over 1,000 years.

Elaeocarpus decipiens.facts: It gets its name from its fragrant, bell-shaped white flowers that bloom in early summer.

Flowering cherry.facts: In many cultures, the brief blooming period of the cherry blossom symbolizes the fleeting nature of life.

Ginkgo biloba.facts: Often called a 'living fossil,' it is the only remaining species in its entire biological division.

Koelreuteria paniculata.facts: After its yellow flowers fall like 'rain,' it grows papery seed pods that look like tiny pink lanterns.

Lagerstroemia indica.facts: Commonly known as the '100-day flower' because its vibrant blooms last all through the summer.

Liquidambar formosana.facts: The resin from this tree is used in traditional medicine, and its leaves turn a deep purple-red in autumn.

Liriodendron chinense.facts: The leaves are shaped like a traditional Chinese jacket (Magua), and the flowers look like green tulips.

Magnolia grandiflora L.facts: This tree produces some of the largest flowers in the world, which can be up to 12 inches across.

Magnolia liliflora Desr.facts: The purple, lily-like flowers usually appear on bare branches before the leaves emerge in spring.

Michelia chapensis.facts: Its flowers are incredibly fragrant and are often used in high-end perfumes and essential oils.

Osmanthus fragrans.facts: The tiny flowers produce a scent so strong it can be smelled from a long distance; they are also used to scent tea.

Photinia serratifolia.facts: The new leaves emerge as a brilliant, fiery red before eventually turning green as they mature.

Platanus.facts: Known for its 'camouflage' bark that flakes off, allowing the tree to shed pollutants and breathe in smoggy cities.

Prunus cerasifera f. atropurpurea.facts: One of the few trees that keeps dark, reddish-purple leaves throughout the entire growing season.

Salix babylonica.facts: The flexible branches were once used to make baskets. Its bark contains salicin, which is chemically similar to aspirin.

Sapindus saponaria.facts: The berries contain saponins, a natural detergent. They can be used as a soap substitute for washing clothes.

Styphnolobium japonicum.facts: Once planted at Buddhist temples, its dried flower buds are used in China as a yellow dye for fine silks.

Triadica sebifera.facts: The seeds are covered in a thick layer of white vegetable tallow (wax) used for making soap and candles.

Zelkova serrata.facts: Highly prized for bonsai, this tree is known for its graceful, fan-like shape and saw-toothed leaves.
